# sha384.sh

Build-time step which replaces every `sha384.sh::path/to/file` marker in html pages with the real
SRI-style hash (`sha384-<base64>`) of that file. It lets a page publish a "download + verify checksum + run"
snippet without hand-maintaining the hash.

```
sha384.sh::pages/node/curl.js   ->   sha384-OdBGfw1BV7BWBiuVl5BDC5KREOG6aHeoK9kCLSvM7rczqmRDoc/u2ViiBp6LmeDy
```

## How it works

Two files:

- `.github/sha384.sh` - driver. `cd` to repo root, collects `find "pages" -type f -name "*.html"` + root
  `index.html`, keeps files containing `sha384\.sh::`, calls the node script once per file.
- `.github/sha384.cjs <file> [--dry-run]` - for each `/sha384\.sh::([^"]+)/g` match hashes the referenced
  file (same result as `openssl dgst -sha384 -binary FILE | base64`) and rewrites the html in place.

Rules that follow from the above:

- the path is **relative to repo root** and ends at the **next `"`** - the marker has to be closed by a
  double quote
- only `*.html` under `pages/` and root `index.html` are scanned - a marker anywhere else is never replaced
- referenced file missing -> node throws -> `sha384.sh` exits 1

Modes:

| call                                                             | effect                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `/bin/bash .github/sha384.sh`                                    | dry-run: validates that referenced files exist only |
| `/bin/bash .github/sha384.sh --run` or `CI=true` (any non-empty) | rewrites html files in place                        |

List files / occurrences which will be processed:

```bash
{ find "pages" -type f -name "*.html"; echo "index.html"; } | xargs grep -l "sha384\.sh::"
{ find "pages" -type f -name "*.html"; echo "index.html"; } | xargs grep -n "sha384\.sh::"
```

## Lifecycle

Only caller is `build.sh` (`make build`, and the `Build` step of `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml`).
There is also a manual `xx sha384` entry in `xx.cjs` (dry-run). The dev server never calls it.

Relevant order in `build.sh` (it runs with `set -e`):

1. `scripts/template.sh` - `*.template.html` -> `*.rendered.html` (marker is copied, so both get replaced)
2. `bash/substitute-variables-bash.sh gitstorage-core.sh` - modifies a file which is later hashed
3. `.github/urlwizzard.sh`, `.github/injector.sh` - may modify hashed `*.sh` / `*.js` (they skip directories
   named `bash`)
4. `prettier --write .` - might reformat hashed `*.js` files
5. **`.github/sha384.sh`** - has to stay after 1-4, so it hashes what will be really served
6. `.github/clicksecure.sh` - touches only html, not the hashed files

- **locally**: no `CI` -> dry-run. Sources keep the markers, pages served locally show the raw marker, so the
  snippets fail the checksum there (expected). A wrong path still breaks the local build.
- **CI**: `CI` is set by GitHub Actions -> files are rewritten in the workspace, tested, deployed to GitHub
  Pages. Nothing is committed back - the repo always holds markers, only the deployed site holds hashes.
- never commit after `--run`: markers would be lost and hashes go stale.

## Where it is used

9 files (6 sources + 3 generated `*.rendered.html`), 10 distinct markers:

| page                                   | hashed file (marker)                           | downloaded to                          | on success               |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `pages/git/index.html`                 | `gitstorage-core.sh`                           | `.git/gitstorage-core.sh`              | `/bin/bash` it           |
| `pages/git/index.html`                 | `bash/git/list-relative-branches.sh`           | `.git/list-relative-branches.sh`       | `/bin/bash` it           |
| `pages/java/index.html`                | `bash/java/gjf.sh`                             | `/usr/local/bin/gjf` (all with `sudo`) | `chmod +x`, run          |
| `pages/bash/index.html`                | `pages/bash/xx/xx.node.bundled.gitignored.cjs` | `~/xx/...`                             | add alias to `~/.bashrc` |
| `pages/bash/index.html`                | `pages/bash/xx/xx.sh`                          | `~/xx/xx.sh`                           | (same block as above)    |
| `pages/bash/index.html`                | `pages/bash/xx/xx-template.cjs`                | `~/xx/xx-template.cjs`                 | (same block as above)    |
| `pages/typescript/index.template.html` | `pages/typescript/tsx.sh`                      | `tsx.sh`                               | print usage              |
| `pages/ai/mcp.template.html`           | `pages/ai/intercept.js`                        | `intercept.js`                         | nothing                  |
| `pages/node/index.template.html`       | `pages/node/engines.js`                        | `engines.js`                           | `node engines.js jest`   |
| `pages/node/index.template.html`       | `pages/node/curl.js`                           | `curl.js`                              | `/bin/bash curl.js`      |

All use the snippet below. Per case only 4 things differ: url, local target, `sudo` or not, success action.
`pages/bash/index.html` (xx) wraps the same snippet in a `download_verified` function and installs only when
all three files pass (`&&`).

## Caveats

- `sha384.sh` has dead code (`S`, the `FIND` heredoc + eval) - harmless.
- `*.rendered.html` are regenerated from templates by `scripts/template.sh` - edit the template, not the
  rendered file.

## Snippet

Everything case specific sits once at the top - url and file name are not repeated across the block.

```bash
URL="urlwizzard.schema://urlwizzard.hostnegotiated/pages/node/curl.js"
FILE="curl.js"
SHA384="sha384.sh::pages/node/curl.js"

if command -v wget > /dev/null; then
  wget --no-cache -O "${FILE}" "${URL}"
else
  curl -fL "${URL}" -o "${FILE}"
fi

if [ "sha384-$(openssl dgst -sha384 -binary "${FILE}" | base64)" = "${SHA384}" ]; then
  echo "checksum verified"
  /bin/bash "${FILE}"
else
  echo "checksum corrupted - deleting file"
  rm -f "${FILE}"
fi
```

What changed and why it is safe on mac and linux:

- `command -v wget` instead of `wget --help` + `$?` - POSIX builtin, same in bash / zsh / sh
- `curl -fL` - `-f` doesn't save a 404 html page as the script, `-L` follows redirects
- `openssl dgst -sha384 -binary FILE | base64` - same tools as before, without `cat` and `printf` wrappers.
  Hash is 64 characters, so linux `base64` line wrapping (76) never kicks in
- `rm -f` - no error when the download failed and there is nothing to delete
- `sudo` case (`pages/java/index.html`): put `sudo` in front of `wget` / `curl` / `openssl` / `rm`
- more files in one go (`pages/bash/index.html`): repeat the block per file, install only when all passed

## Snippet - execute only

Safe replacement for `curl ... | bash`: download to a temporary file, verify, pass to bash only when verified,
nothing is left on the disk. Only the first two lines change, arguments for the script go after `"${FILE}"`.

```bash
URL="urlwizzard.schema://urlwizzard.hostnegotiated/pages/node/curl.js"
SHA384="sha384.sh::pages/node/curl.js"
FILE="$(mktemp)"

if command -v wget > /dev/null; then
  wget --no-cache -O "${FILE}" "${URL}"
else
  curl -fL "${URL}" -o "${FILE}"
fi

if [ "sha384-$(openssl dgst -sha384 -binary "${FILE}" | base64)" = "${SHA384}" ]; then
  echo "checksum verified"
  /bin/bash "${FILE}"
else
  echo "checksum corrupted - not executing"
fi

rm -f "${FILE}"
```

A temporary file (not a shell variable or a pipe) is used on purpose: `$(...)` strips trailing newlines, which
changes the hash, and a pipe would start executing before the whole file is verified.
